product_concept: A focused guide / checklist that helps People overwhelmed by their to-do list a daily ritual that surfaces the 1-3 things that truly matter.
target_customer: People overwhelmed by their to-do list
core_problem: People overwhelmed by their to-do list face a related cluster of problems around prioritization & daily focus system — e.g. no prioritization on the list, task paralysis from overwhelm, quick vs big tasks not separated.
related_problems: Everything lands on one undifferentiated list, so nothing feels urgent and the brain defaults to the easiest task.
Too many tasks at once triggers overwhelm and freeze — people can't decide where to start (task paralysis).
No differentiation between quick tasks and big projects, so important deep work is deferred.
desired_outcome: A daily ritual that surfaces the 1-3 things that truly matter.
core_transformation: From: People overwhelmed by their to-do list face a related cluster of problems around prioritization & daily focus system — e.g. no prioritization on the list, task paralysis from overwhelm, quick vs big tasks not separated.  →  To: A daily ritual that surfaces the 1-3 things that truly matter.
product_promise: Get to 'A daily ritual that surfaces the 1-3 things that truly matter.' without the usual guesswork.
product_format: Bundle: Single 'Must-Do' active display mode + Secondary backlog drawer (hidden during execution) + Random task spinner/die button to bypass decision freeze
why_this_format: Mechanism → format: Single-task focus view coupled with a 2-tier backlog filter and a 1-click randomizer tool.. Users report success with 1 must-do focus and dice rolling, but express frustration with heavy apps; thus format must be minimalist. (basis: inferred)
product_structure: 1-Must-Do Focus View — Isolate the primary priority so the user is not overwhelmed by secondary tasks. [observed]
Randomized Task Selector ('Roll the Dice') — Break active task paralysis and decision freeze through forced arbitrary choice. [observed]
Secondary Backlog Vault — Store non-urgent or non-essential tasks out of daily line of sight. [observed]
exclude: Complex multi-tagging, nested folder hierarchies, or Kanban boards
Unrestricted visible backlog lists on the primary screen
Heavy analytics dashboards or friction-heavy setup wizards
differentiation: A minimalist single-focus ritual app that limits active daily tasks to 1-3 items, relegates all other entries to an out-of-sight secondary vault, and includes a single-button randomized selector for paralysis moments.
price_rationale: Pricing UNKNOWN; do not set a price until validated.
key_customer_language: Everything lands on one undifferentiated list, so nothing feels urgent and the brain defaults to the easiest task.
Too many tasks at once triggers overwhelm and freeze — people can't decide where to start (task paralysis).
No differentiation between quick tasks and big projects, so important deep work is deferred.
key_objections: Templates never fit my exact case
evidence_summary: Outcome: READY. 163 results discovered → 92 candidates → 0 retrieved → 5 evidence-bearing. Mechanism: Single-task focus view coupled with a 2-tier backlog filter and a 1-click randomizer tool.
risks_unknowns: Willingness to pay and monetization viability remain completely unknown.
